message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and use an AAA diagnosis endpoint (phenotyping_reported). Among them, PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet GWAS meta-analysis) is best supported by study archetype and endpoint fidelity: it comes from a dedicated AAA genome-wide association meta-analysis with many contributing cohorts (multi-cohort, disease-focused), which the provided domain_knowledge prioritizes over portability/pan-trait frameworks when endpoints are comparable. Competing models have notable limitations in the visible metadata: PGS002054 is explicitly from a UKB portability framework paper and reports only partial-r (not directly comparable to AUROC/R2); PGS001784 is from a global biobank framework and its listed AUROC=0.868 is a full-model metric with substantial covariates (age/age^2/interaction terms/20 PCs), while its PGS-only R2 is small (0.0147), suggesting the high AUROC is largely covariate-driven per the heritability sanity-check guidance; PGS003429 is a screening/cost-effectiveness context with unknown covariates and modest AUROC (0.708); PGS000753 is older, very sparse (29 variants), and provides only an OR per SD (1.37) without AUC/R2. Remaining limitation: PGS003972 itself only reports a full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates and lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2, and there is an unresolved discrepancy with PGS003973 (same publication/method/variant count) reporting a much higher full-model C-index (0.882) but with a different covariate set—without PRS-only/incremental metrics, these full-model values are not safely comparable, so confidence cannot be high."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have acceptable endpoint fidelity (all report abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent but still aligned). Several are framework-style scores (PGS001784 from a global biobank portability paper; PGS002054 from a UKB portability paper) which domain guidance suggests down-ranking when disease-focused alternatives exist. Among disease-focused candidates, PGS003972/PGS003973 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis) provide the strongest disease-specific, multi-cohort development context; between them, PGS003973 reports a higher full-model C-index (0.882) but it is not a PRS-only metric and could be largely covariate-driven, whereas PGS003972 reports AUROC=0.69 with covariates unknown; neither provides PRS-only discrimination. I select PGS003972 as the best-supported disease-focused multi-cohort PRS-CS model without relying on an outlier full-model metric, but confidence is low because performance reporting is non-comparable across candidates (mix of full-model metrics, partial-r, and effect size only), covariates are unknown for key models, and the PGS-only contribution cannot be cleanly separated for the leading candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and use an AAA disease endpoint in phenotyping_reported (one is prevalent AAA, others are generic AAA), so selection hinges on study archetype + endpoint fidelity + PRS-comparable performance evidence. PGS003972 comes from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed) with a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) and European evaluation, aligning with domain guidance to prefer disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analyses for cardiovascular/large-vessel diseases over portability/framework scores. Competing options have notable limitations: PGS001784 is a global biobank framework score (Cell Genom) with only modest covariates-regressed-out R2 (0.014661) and a high full-model AUROC (0.868) that is not PRS-only; PGS002054 is explicitly a UKB portability framework (partial-r 0.0144 only); PGS000753 is older, ultra-sparse (29 variants) and uses a prevalent endpoint with no AUC/R2 (only OR=1.37 per SD). Between the two Nat Genet PRS-CS models (PGS003972 and PGS003973), the very high C-index reported for PGS003973 (0.882) is difficult to interpret as PRS contribution because it appears as a full-model metric and is an outlier relative to the other AAA models; PGS003972’s AUROC=0.69 is more plausible and avoids over-weighting a potentially covariate-driven or otherwise non-comparable high full-model metric. Confidence is only moderate because key PRS-only or incremental metrics are missing for most candidates, covariates are unknown for PGS003972, and the PGS003972 vs PGS003973 choice remains somewhat ambiguous given both share the same publication and method family."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm, with one explicitly “prevalent” but still endpoint-faithful). PGS000753 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused abdominal aortic aneurysm genetic architecture study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) and provides a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), which is interpretable as PRS contribution evidence rather than relying on potentially covariate-driven full-model discrimination. Competing options either (i) are framework/portability-style scores (PGS001784 ‘Global Biobank…’; PGS002054 ‘Portability of 245…’) where reported metrics are less directly attributable to PRS utility for this specific disease, or (ii) report only full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown/limited covariate detail (PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973), making cross-model comparison and PRS-specific attribution uncertain. Limitation: several candidates have much larger validation samples and/or higher reported full-model AUROC/C-index, but PRS-only or incremental metrics are largely missing across models, and at least one very high full-model metric (e.g., C-index 0.882 in PGS003973) may be substantially covariate-driven; therefore the ‘best’ choice is not unambiguous from the visible evidence, lowering confidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (all are abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is explicitly prevalent AAA). For selection, the most disease-focused, multi-cohort GWAS meta-analysis-derived options are the Nat Genet AAA scores (PGS003972/PGS003973), which align with the domain policy favoring cardiovascular large-vessel disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analyses over portability/framework scores and over older sparse prevalent-only models. Between these two near-sibling models, PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from the same dedicated AAA meta-analysis context with broader listed contributing cohorts (includes UKB and VIVA in the provided cohort list) and has a simpler/basic covariate set listed as unknown (not obviously clinically leakage-heavy), while the apparent performance edge of PGS003973 (C-index 0.882) is a full-model metric that is not directly comparable to PGS-only discrimination and is likely strongly driven by age/sex for AAA; PGS003972’s reported AUROC (0.69) is also full-model but less likely to be misinterpreted as exceptional PRS lift. Confidence is not high because neither Nat Genet model reports an explicit PGS-only AUROC/R2 or incremental metrics, covariates are missing/unknown for PGS003972, and other direct-match candidates have much larger validation samples (e.g., PGS001784) albeit from a framework-style global biobank paper whose full-model AUROC is also not PRS-only."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported strings for abdominal aortic aneurysm (one is explicitly prevalent; others are generic AAA). Among them, PGS000753 is from a disease-focused AAA publication (MVP/Mayo context) and reports a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), providing PRS-specific discriminative signal without relying on potentially covariate-driven full-model AUROC. Competing candidates either come from framework/portability-style studies (PGS001784; PGS002054) where reported metrics are not clearly PRS-only and can be harder to compare, or report only full-model discrimination with unknown covariates (PGS003429, PGS003972) or very high C-index with only basic covariates but without PRS-only/incremental metrics (PGS003973), making it unclear how much of the discrimination is attributable to the PRS. Confidence is limited because across models the most comparable PRS-only metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) are largely missing, and several candidates have strong but non-comparable full-model metrics, preventing a clearly definitive best choice."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and all report an abdominal aortic aneurysm endpoint in phenotyping_reported (one is explicitly prevalent: PGS000753; others are generic AAA). Among disease-focused candidates, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet) with broad multi-cohort development, which domain guidance suggests should generally be preferred over pan-trait/framework scores (e.g., PGS001784 ‘Global Biobank…’ and PGS002054 ‘Portability of 245…’) when endpoint fidelity is comparable. Between the two Nat Genet PRS-CS models, PGS003972 has cleaner/less potentially covariate-driven reporting (AUROC=0.69 with covariates unknown) than PGS003973, whose very high C-index (0.882) is reported alongside age/age^2/sex covariates and could be largely covariate-driven rather than PRS-driven per the provided policy; moreover neither provides explicit PGS-only metrics to isolate PRS contribution. This yields a preference for PGS003972, but confidence is limited by missing PRS-only AUROC/R2, unknown covariates for PGS003972, and the lack of directly comparable performance metrics across candidates (e.g., PGS000753 provides OR per SD but no AUROC/R2; framework models provide different metric types)."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait/efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping strings for AAA (PGS000753 explicitly prevalent; others generic AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA; one is prevalent AAA). Two candidates (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis publication (Nat Genet 2023) with multi-cohort development, which domain guidance favors over pan-trait/portability frameworks when endpoints are comparable. Between those two, PGS003973 reports a high full-model C-index (0.882) but this is likely dominated by covariates (Age, Age^2, Sex) and is not a PRS-only metric; PGS003972 reports a lower full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates. Given the policy to avoid letting a single full-model metric dominate and to prefer the strongest disease-focused evidence package when metrics are non-comparable/underspecified, I select PGS003972 as the more conservative representative from the same disease-focused study family. Confidence is only moderate because key PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUC) are missing across the leading disease-focused options, covariates are unknown for PGS003972, and large validation + PRS-only R2 is available for a framework model (PGS001784) but is penalized by its pan-trait context and covariate-heavy full-model AUROC."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm endpoints, with one explicitly prevalent AAA for PGS000753). Among the more disease-focused, multi-cohort AAA efforts, PGS003972/PGS003973 (Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis; PRS-CS; many contributing cohorts) provide the strongest endpoint/study-context support versus framework-style scores (PGS001784 global biobank PRS and PGS002054 UKB portability paper) and versus the smaller, sparse P+T MVP-era score (PGS000753). Between the two Nat Genet PRS-CS options, PGS003973 reports a very high full-model C-index (0.882) but with limited PRS-isolated performance metrics and only basic covariates; given domain guidance not to over-rank based on a single full-model metric (especially when PRS-only AUROC is absent) and the lack of incremental/PRS-only metrics for both, PGS003972 is selected as the more conservative choice with a more typical reported AUROC (0.69) for European validation. Main limitation: performance reporting is not directly comparable across candidates (several have only full-model AUROC/C-index or partial-r, and PRS-only AUROC is generally missing), so the preference is driven primarily by phenotype fidelity and disease-focused multi-cohort study context rather than clean head-to-head PRS metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All six candidates are direct EFO matches to age-related macular degeneration, but they differ in endpoint fidelity and the interpretability/comparability of reported performance. PGS004606 has strong phenotype alignment (phenotyping_reported: Age-related macular degeneration), is from a disease-focused AMD GWAS/meta-analysis context (IAMDGC; Nat Genet 2024), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) with large-scale evaluation (validation_sample_size n=163,011, EUR), and reports an AUROC=0.71 with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10), making it the most consistently supported package among the visible options. Key limitation: the AUROC appears as a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only/incremental), and competing models either (i) come from a portability framework with only weak partial-r (~0.016–0.018; PGS001834/PGS002041), (ii) have endpoint mismatch/proxy phenotype issues (PGS002269 phenotyping is retinal layer thickness despite AMD label), or (iii) show a high AUROC in a very small validation set and possible reporting inconsistency (PGS004952: n=1,232; AUROC shown as 84.2 vs 0.842). Because PRS-only performance is not clearly isolated for the top candidate and there is metric/reporting ambiguity in the set, the direct-match recommendation is best-effort but not high-certainty."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 4 candidates are direct matches in concept to alcohol dependence, but they differ in endpoint labeling and evidence completeness. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All four candidates are direct/near-direct matches to alcohol dependence via closely aligned endpoints (PGS002738/PGS002739: trait_efo=alcohol dependence, phenotyping_reported=Alcohol use disorder; PGS000201/PGS000202: trait_efo=alcohol dependence measurement with DSM-5 AUD criteria count).
